In [[mathematics|mathematical]] [[set theory]], a '''pseudo-intersection''' of a family of sets is an [[infinite set]] ''S'' such that each element of the family contains all but a finite number of elements of ''S''. The '''pseudo-intersection number''', sometimes denoted by the [[fraktur]] letter 𝔭, is the smallest size of a family of infinite subsets of the natural numbers that has the [[strong finite intersection property]] but has no pseudo-intersection.
